_comment: 10e Pariah Nexus tournament-pack Fixed Secondary Missions. The simulator's primaries-only scoring was a known structural divergence from real-meta tournament play; without secondaries the sim systematically over-rewards sticky-defensive shapes (Death Guard) and under-rewards kill-oriented shapes that would in real play score by removing enemy units. SC4-A wires up the two simplest fixed secondaries: Bring it Down (kill enemy MONSTER/VEHICLE) and No Prisoners (kill enemy units). Source: https://wahapedia.ru/wh40k10ed/the-rules/pariah-nexus-mission-pack/

simulator.secondary_cleanse.rule_name: Cleanse (Pariah Nexus Tactical/Fixed Secondary Mission — action-based)
simulator.secondary_cleanse.quoted_text: Cleanse scores 2 VP if you cleanse (Action) one objective marker outside your deployment zone, and 4 VP if you cleanse two. The action requires one or more units in range of different objective markers not in your deployment zone, and it completes at the end of your turn. Each unit cleanses a single objective marker. (Wahapedia DNS was unreachable from this environment; verified via the Goonhammer Pariah Nexus mission review and a corroborating web search of the GW pack.)
simulator.secondary_cleanse.trigger: After the Movement phase, a surplus unit (cheap, spare-able 'chaff' per strategy._is_chaff_unit) sitting on an objective its army CONTROLS that is OUTSIDE its own deployment zone performs the Cleanse action. While performing it the unit cannot shoot or declare a charge (lockout in Battle._do_shoot / _do_charge). At end of turn the action scores if the unit survived and the army still controls that objective.
simulator.secondary_cleanse.effect: 2 VP per cleansed objective marker (outside the scoring army's deployment zone, controlled, with a surviving Cleanse unit), capped at two objectives (4 VP per turn). The shoot/charge lockout is the action-vs-fight tradeoff: a low-model durable army has no chaff to spare and never satisfies it, while a horde / MSU army does — an even-handed counterbalance to the kill-secondary asymmetry that falls out of unit cost, not faction. Implemented in Battle._assign_cleanse_actions / _score_cleanse.

simulator.secondary_sabotage.rule_name: Sabotage (Pariah Nexus Tactical Secondary Mission — action-based)
simulator.secondary_sabotage.quoted_text: Sabotage: one of your units outside your deployment zone can start this action in the Shooting phase, which finishes at the end of your opponent's next turn or the end of the battle. You complete the action in No Man's Land for 3 VP or in your opponent's deployment zone for 6 VP. (Wahapedia DNS unreachable; verified via the Goonhammer Pariah Nexus mission review and a corroborating web search of the GW pack.)
simulator.secondary_sabotage.trigger: After the Movement phase, a surplus chaff unit (per strategy._is_chaff_unit) that is OUTSIDE its own deployment zone (in No Man's Land or the enemy deployment zone) performs the Sabotage action; it cannot shoot or charge that turn (the action-vs-fight tradeoff). At end of round the action scores if the unit survived forward (an approximation of 'completes at end of opponent's next turn'); a unit shot off mid-round scores nothing.
simulator.secondary_sabotage.effect: The best surviving Sabotage completes for 6 VP in the enemy deployment zone or 3 VP in No Man's Land, capped at one completion (6 VP) per round (SwegHammer simplification — a conservative cap on a deliberately risky deep-push action). Rewards pushing expendable bodies forward, which a deepstrike / infiltrate under-shooter does and a durable low-model camper cannot. Implemented in Battle._assign_sabotage_actions / _score_sabotage.

simulator.secondary_vp_cap_40.quoted_text: Players add up their points from Secondary Missions and can score a maximum of 40 VP from these. If a player is using Fixed Missions they can score a maximum of 20 VP from each one of the missions.
simulator.secondary_vp_cap_40.trigger: End of game, when deciding the winner. SwegHammer's running _a_vp/_b_vp totals mix primary and secondary VP and never enforced the 40-VP secondary ceiling, so secondary-heavy shapes (Custodes ~39 secondary VP/game) could exceed it.
simulator.secondary_vp_cap_40.effect: The win condition (Battle._decide_winner) decides on primary VP plus min(secondary VP, 40), enforcing the real 40-VP total-secondary ceiling. Uses the per-side _a_secondary_vp / _b_secondary_vp tally (otherwise a reporting accumulator). Env-gated SWEG_S2 for the wave-75 A/B.

simulator.secondary_bring_it_down.source: https://wahapedia.ru/wh40k10ed/the-rules/chapter-approved-2025-26/ (Chapter Approved 2025-26 deck; cross-checked vs Goonhammer CA-2025 review + GW Tournament Companion, wave 92)
simulator.secondary_bring_it_down.rule_name: Bring It Down (Chapter Approved 2025-26 Secondary Mission, Fixed)
simulator.secondary_bring_it_down.quoted_text: Each time an enemy MONSTER or VEHICLE unit is destroyed, score 2VP. If the total Wounds characteristic of that unit was 15 or more, score an extra 2VP. If 20 or more, score a further 2VP. Maximum 6VP per unit. [No per-turn cap.]
simulator.secondary_bring_it_down.trigger: end of each battle round, when computing the round-end delta of an army's destroyed MONSTER/VEHICLE units against the opponent's round-start snapshot
simulator.secondary_bring_it_down.effect: 2 VP base + 2 (15+ total wounds) + 2 (20+) per destroyed MONSTER/VEHICLE, capped at 6 per unit (CA-2025-26 Fixed; was modelled as a flat 3 per model). No per-round cap (the 18 ceiling does not bind; the 40-VP secondary total cap bounds it). Uses the destroyed model's Wounds characteristic (profile.health) — for single-model MONSTER/VEHICLE (most) this equals the unit total; multi-model squadrons under-count (rare, accepted).

simulator.secondary_no_prisoners.source: https://wahapedia.ru/wh40k10ed/the-rules/chapter-approved-2025-26/ (Chapter Approved 2025-26 deck — the deck the May-2026 calibration target was played under; values cross-checked vs Goonhammer CA-2025 review + GW Tournament Companion, wave 91)
simulator.secondary_no_prisoners.rule_name: No Prisoners (Chapter Approved 2025-26 Secondary Mission, Tactical only — banned as a Fixed pick in tournament play)
simulator.secondary_no_prisoners.quoted_text: Each time an enemy unit is destroyed, score 2VP (up to a maximum of 5VP per turn). [Fixed version narrows to Bodyguard / non-CHARACTER units and is banned as a Fixed pick in tournament play; the simulator scores the per-unit 2 VP form.]
simulator.secondary_no_prisoners.trigger: end of each battle round, when computing the round-end delta of an army's destroyed units against the opponent's round-start snapshot
simulator.secondary_no_prisoners.effect: the opposing army gains 2 VP per destroyed enemy unit this round, capped at 5 VP per round (CA-2025-26 value; was a stale 5/15 in the citation and 3/5 in code).

simulator.secondary_engage_on_all_fronts.source: https://wahapedia.ru/wh40k10ed/the-rules/chapter-approved-2025-26/ (Chapter Approved 2025-26 deck — the deck the May-2026 calibration target was played under; values cross-checked vs Goonhammer CA-2025 review + GW Tournament Companion, wave 91)
simulator.secondary_engage_on_all_fronts.rule_name: Engage on All Fronts (Chapter Approved 2025-26 Secondary Mission)
simulator.secondary_engage_on_all_fronts.quoted_text: Score 1VP if you have one or more units wholly within two table quarters; 2VP instead for three different table quarters; 4VP instead for all four table quarters.
simulator.secondary_engage_on_all_fronts.trigger: end of each battle round, evaluating each side's alive-unit quadrant coverage
simulator.secondary_engage_on_all_fronts.effect: 1 / 2 / 4 VP for alive units occupying 2 / 3 / 4 of the table quarters (CA-2025-26; was Pariah Nexus 2/3/5 — CA-2025-26 adds a 1-VP floor at 2 quarters and lowers the 3/4-quarter tiers).

simulator.secondary_behind_enemy_lines.source: https://wahapedia.ru/wh40k10ed/the-rules/chapter-approved-2025-26/ (Chapter Approved 2025-26 deck — the deck the May-2026 calibration target was played under; values cross-checked vs Goonhammer CA-2025 review + GW Tournament Companion, wave 91)
simulator.secondary_behind_enemy_lines.rule_name: Behind Enemy Lines (Chapter Approved 2025-26 Secondary Mission)
simulator.secondary_behind_enemy_lines.quoted_text: Score 3VP if one non-AIRCRAFT unit from your army is wholly within your opponent's deployment zone; score 4VP instead if two or more are. [Unchanged from Pariah Nexus.]
simulator.secondary_behind_enemy_lines.trigger: end of each battle round, evaluating each side's alive-unit positions against the opponent's deployment-zone strip
simulator.secondary_behind_enemy_lines.effect: 3 VP if exactly one alive unit is within the opponent's deployment zone, 4 VP if two or more (CA-2025-26; the sim previously modelled a flat 4).

simulator.secondary_cull_the_horde.source: https://wahapedia.ru/wh40k10ed/the-rules/chapter-approved-2025-26/ (Chapter Approved 2025-26 deck — the deck the May-2026 calibration target was played under; values cross-checked vs Goonhammer CA-2025 review + GW Tournament Companion, wave 91)
simulator.secondary_cull_the_horde.rule_name: Cull the Horde (Chapter Approved 2025-26 Secondary Mission)
simulator.secondary_cull_the_horde.quoted_text: Each time an enemy INFANTRY unit with a Starting Strength of 13 or more (including any attached units) is destroyed, score 5VP. [No per-turn cap.]
simulator.secondary_cull_the_horde.trigger: end of each battle round, when an enemy unit whose starting strength was 10+ was destroyed this round
simulator.secondary_cull_the_horde.effect: 5 VP per qualifying INFANTRY unit destroyed whose Starting Strength was 13+ (CA-2025-26; was Pariah Nexus 20+/25-wounds, sim previously 10+ at 3 VP). No per-round cap (the sim's 15 ceiling does not bind in practice; the 40-VP secondary total cap bounds it). The 'including attached Leaders' clause is approximated by the squad's starting model count.

simulator.warlord_designation.source: https://wahapedia.ru/wh40k10ed/the-rules/chapter-approved-2025-26/ (Chapter Approved 2025-26 deck; cross-checked vs Goonhammer CA-2025 review + GW Tournament Companion, wave 92)
simulator.warlord_designation.rule_name: Warlord designation + Pariah Nexus Assassination bonus
simulator.warlord_designation.quoted_text: Each player must select one CHARACTER model in their army to be their Warlord. Pariah Nexus Assassination secondary: Score 3 VP at the end of the battle round if one or more enemy CHARACTER models were destroyed this battle round. Score 4 VP instead if the enemy WARLORD was among those models.
simulator.warlord_designation.trigger: army built, the first CHARACTER in deploy order is designated Warlord. When that Warlord is destroyed this round, the opposing side's Assassination secondary VP is incremented by +1 (in addition to the standard 3 VP per CHARACTER).
simulator.warlord_designation.effect: Army.warlord_uid is lazily set to the first CHARACTER unit in deploy order (faction-neutral, deterministic). CHAPTER APPROVED 2025-26 UPDATE: Assassination no longer grants a Warlord bonus (the +1 was removed), so ASSASSINATION_WARLORD_BONUS_VP is 0 and the Warlord designation no longer affects Assassination scoring; the designation is retained for API stability and any future Warlord-keyed rule.

simulator.tactical_secondary_deck_draw.quoted_text: At the start of the battle, each player creates a Tactical Mission deck of 9 Secondary Mission cards. At the start of their first turn, each player draws 2 Tactical Mission cards from their deck. From each subsequent battle round onwards, each player draws back up to 2 Tactical Mission cards at the start of their turn.
simulator.tactical_secondary_deck_draw.trigger: end of each battle round, when scoring tactical secondaries (Engage on All Fronts, Behind Enemy Lines) per side
simulator.tactical_secondary_deck_draw.effect: each side scores AT MOST ONE of the implemented tactical secondaries per round, alternating between Engage and BEL on a deterministic schedule keyed by (round_num, side). LC-2 APPROXIMATION: real Pariah Nexus has 9 Tactical cards; SwegHammer implements 2 (Engage + BEL). Without gating, both would score every round (100% coverage) — which over-rewarded elite low-count factions that easily hit the conditions. The alternating deterministic draw scales coverage to ~50% per side per round per card, approximating the real 2-of-9 ~22% rate when scaled to a 2-card pool. Cited as `simulator.tactical_secondary_deck_draw`.

simulator.tactical_secondary_deck.source: https://wahapedia.ru/wh40k10ed/the-rules/chapter-approved-2025-26/ (Chapter Approved 2025-26 deck — the deck the May-2026 calibration target was played under; deck mechanic cross-checked vs the Pariah Nexus Tactical Mission rules + Goonhammer CA-2025 review)
simulator.tactical_secondary_deck.rule_name: Secondary Missions — Fixed vs Tactical, and the Tactical deck draw/achieve/redraw mechanic (Chapter Approved 2025-26)
simulator.tactical_secondary_deck.quoted_text: When you muster your army, you must decide whether you will be using Fixed Missions or Tactical Missions for the battle. ... If you are using Tactical Missions: At the start of your first Command phase, draw two cards from your Secondary Mission deck. Those two Secondary Missions are active for you until you achieve them. At the start of each of your subsequent Command phases, if you have fewer than two active Secondary Mission cards, draw Secondary Mission cards until you have two active Secondary Mission cards. ... At the end of your turn, if you scored one or more victory points from a Secondary Mission card this turn, that Secondary Mission is achieved; discard that card.
simulator.tactical_secondary_deck.trigger: battle start (track choice from unit count — even-handed, no faction tag) and each Command phase / round end (a TACTICAL army holds at most two active cards, scores only those, and discards+redraws any it scored 1+ VP from)
simulator.tactical_secondary_deck.effect: Replaces the simulator's legacy union-of-~9-11-sources secondary scoring with the real rule: each army uses ONE track. A FIXED army (low unit/chaff count — emergently the Knight) scores its 2 kill cards every round; a TACTICAL army (broad roster with spare chaff) holds a deterministically-seeded 2-card hand drawn from the Tactical/action/board pool, scoring only the hand and running achieve->discard->redraw each round. Bounded by the existing 40-VP secondary total cap. Env-gated SWEG_TAC_DECK; OFF reproduces the legacy scoring byte-for-byte. Even-handed: the Fixed/Tactical split falls out of `secondaries._choose_secondary_track` (chaff + unit count), never a faction. Deterministic: the deck shuffle is seeded from a battle-stable global-RNG draw XOR the army-name CRC, reproducible under PYTHONHASHSEED=0. Implemented as Battle._init_tactical_deck / _score_one_card / _score_tactical_hand / _score_secondaries_deck and secondaries.pick_secondaries / TACTICAL_DECK_POOL. STAGE C TODO: the CA-2025-26 Tactical deck also has action cards (Establish Locus, Recover Assets, A Tempting Target) the sim does not yet model — left as a cited TODO, not invented.

simulator.tactical_voluntary_discard.source: https://wahapedia.ru/wh40k10ed/the-rules/chapter-approved-2025-26/ (Chapter Approved 2025-26 Tactical Missions end-of-turn rule; re-verified verbatim this session, 2026-07-02)
simulator.tactical_voluntary_discard.rule_name: Tactical Missions end-of-turn voluntary discard (Chapter Approved 2025-26)
simulator.tactical_voluntary_discard.quoted_text: At the end of each player's turn, each player using Tactical Missions does the following... First, if you scored 1 or more VP from a Secondary Mission card, discard that card – it is achieved. Then, you can discard one or more of your active Secondary Mission cards. If you do, and it is your turn, you gain 1CP.
simulator.tactical_voluntary_discard.trigger: end of each battle round, inside Battle._score_tactical_hand, immediately after the pre-existing achieved-card discard step, for a TACTICAL-track army's remaining active hand cards. Env-gated SWEG_TAC_VOLUNTARY_DISCARD (default off).
simulator.tactical_voluntary_discard.effect: Implements the second half of the verbatim rule, which the simulator previously left out entirely (only the achieved-card discard from the same sentence was wired up). WHICH card to voluntarily discard is not specified by the rule itself and is decided by an ARTIFICIAL-INTELLIGENCE piloting heuristic, not the rule: a card becomes a candidate once it has been held un-achieved for at least one full previous round (tracked per-card in Army.tactical_hand_age) and scored zero victory points this round (guaranteed for every card still in hand once the achieved-discard step above has run); among candidates the longest-held card is discarded, ties broken by card key for determinism. The card goes to the discard pile (not back into the deck) and the hand refills at the existing redraw step exactly as an achieved card would. At most ONE voluntary discard per turn is modelled, a conservative reading of the rule's 'one or more' (real players rarely dump both active cards at once). The command point is granted unconditionally to the discarding army: the simulator's round model collapses both players' turns into a single interleaved round rather than modelling alternating per-player turns, so each army's own hand-management at round end already stands in for the end of THAT army's own turn, the same approximation the pre-existing achieved-card discard makes turn-agnostically ('if it is your turn' is therefore always true from the discarding army's own perspective in this model). Command points are capped at the universal CP_CAP=6. The discard decision is a pure, deterministic function of card state (no dice); card draws remain on `_init_tactical_deck`'s private zlib.crc32-seeded Random stream, untouched by this change. D1b (SWEG_TAC_SHEDDING, secondary-economy audit fix wave, default ON) folds this voluntary discard into production default-on: when SWEG_TAC_SHEDDING is on, `_score_tactical_hand`'s round-end block runs by default (the SWEG_TAC_VOLUNTARY_DISCARD env var still forces it on independently) and its eligibility test switches from the age>=1 trigger to the achievability read `_tac_discard_card_cannot_pay` (a card that can never score again, or has read zero for a full previous round), per docs/_SEC_ECONOMY_AUDIT.md §7 item 1b. The New Orders Core Stratagem (1 command point: end of your Command phase, discard one active Secondary Mission card and draw one new one) IS now implemented as D1c under the same gate — see `simulator.new_orders_stratagem`. Implemented in Battle._score_tactical_hand / Army.tactical_hand_age. SWEG_SECONDARY_PURSUIT refinement (part (c) of that package gate, which IMPLIES this gate): on the vanilla per-player-turn path, the command-point grant moves from this round-end method (which cannot distinguish either army's turn from the other's, so the base gate above grants unconditionally) to Battle._apply_tactical_voluntary_discard_own_turn, called once per army from _run_round_vanilla_turns at the true end of that army's own turn — a genuine 'if it is your turn' read using the active/other context that function already tracks. The discard heuristic is also replaced: instead of the age>=1 trigger above, Battle._tac_discard_card_cannot_pay requires the candidate card to be either structurally incapable of ever paying in this matchup (no qualifying kill target, marker, or Objective-Control-capable body left, where a cheap structural test exists) or to have read zero for a full previous round (for the remaining cards), per the secondary-economy diagnosis that the tactical track's real bottleneck is card ACHIEVABILITY, not merely hand turnover speed. SWEG_TAC_VOLUNTARY_DISCARD's own environment variable keeps the original unconditional-grant / age-only behaviour documented above, unchanged, whenever the package gate is off.

simulator.secondary_assassination.source: https://wahapedia.ru/wh40k10ed/the-rules/chapter-approved-2025-26/ (Chapter Approved 2025-26 deck; cross-checked vs Goonhammer CA-2025 review + GW Tournament Companion, wave 92)
simulator.secondary_assassination.quoted_text: Each time an enemy CHARACTER model is destroyed, score 4VP if that CHARACTER had a Wounds characteristic of 4 or more, or 3VP if it had fewer than 4. [No per-turn cap; CA-2025-26 has no Warlord bonus.]
simulator.secondary_assassination.trigger: end of each battle round, when an enemy CHARACTER-keyword unit was destroyed this round
simulator.secondary_assassination.effect: 4 VP per destroyed CHARACTER with 4+ Wounds, 3 VP for one with fewer than 4 (CA-2025-26 wound-tier; was a flat 3 per CHARACTER). No per-round cap (12 ceiling, under the 40-VP total). The Pariah Nexus Warlord bonus is removed (set to 0).

simulator.secondary_secure_no_mans_land.rule_name: Secure No Man's Land (Pariah Nexus Secondary Mission)
simulator.secondary_secure_no_mans_land.quoted_text: Secure No Man's Land: 2VP if controlling one objective marker in No Man's Land; or 5VP if controlling two or more objective markers in No Man's Land.
simulator.secondary_secure_no_mans_land.trigger: end of each battle round, counting the No Man's Land objective markers (outside both deployment zones) the scoring army controls (strictly greater Objective Control than the opponent within the marker's radius)
simulator.secondary_secure_no_mans_land.effect: 2 VP for one controlled No Man's Land objective, 5 VP for two or more. Implemented in Battle._score_board_secondaries (env-gated SWEG_TIER_A). Rewards a body army that can spread across the midboard, which a low-model durable camper cannot — even-handed (same pool + scoring both sides; the asymmetry is in completion, bounded by the 40-VP secondary cap).

simulator.secondary_defend_stronghold.quoted_text: Defend Stronghold: 3VP if controlling one or more objective markers in your deployment zone.
simulator.secondary_defend_stronghold.trigger: end of each battle round, when the scoring army controls one or more objective markers in its own deployment zone
simulator.secondary_defend_stronghold.effect: 3 VP. Implemented in Battle._score_board_secondaries (env-gated SWEG_TIER_A). Available to every army (a camper holding its home objective scores it too) — even-handed.

simulator.secondary_extend_battle_lines.source: https://wahapedia.ru/wh40k10ed/the-rules/chapter-approved-2025-26/ (Chapter Approved 2025-26 deck — the deck the May-2026 calibration target was played under; values cross-checked vs Goonhammer CA-2025 review + GW Tournament Companion, wave 91)
simulator.secondary_extend_battle_lines.rule_name: Extend Battle Lines (Chapter Approved 2025-26 Secondary Mission)
simulator.secondary_extend_battle_lines.quoted_text: Control one or more objective markers in your deployment zone AND one or more in No Man's Land: score 4VP. (CA-2025-26 reduced the top tier from the Pariah Nexus 5 VP to 4 VP.)
simulator.secondary_extend_battle_lines.trigger: end of each battle round, when the scoring army controls at least one objective in its own deployment zone AND at least one in No Man's Land
simulator.secondary_extend_battle_lines.effect: 4 VP for controlling one+ own-deployment-zone objective AND one+ No Man's Land objective (CA-2025-26; reduced from the Pariah Nexus 5). Implemented in Battle._score_board_secondaries.

simulator.secondary_storm_hostile_object.rule_name: Storm Hostile Objective (Pariah Nexus Secondary Mission)
simulator.secondary_storm_hostile_object.quoted_text: Storm Hostile Objective: 4VP if controlling one or more objective markers your opponent controlled at the start of your turn; or (from the second battle round) 4VP if your opponent controlled no objective markers at the start of your turn and you control one or more that you did not control at the start of your turn. APPROXIMATION: SwegHammer scores the first clause — control at round end one or more markers the opponent controlled at round start (captured in _obj_controller_at_round_start); the second alternate clause is not modelled.
simulator.secondary_storm_hostile_object.trigger: end of each battle round, when the scoring army controls one or more objective markers that the opponent controlled at the start of the round
simulator.secondary_storm_hostile_object.effect: 4 VP. Implemented in Battle._score_board_secondaries (env-gated SWEG_TIER_A). This is the scoring REWARD for taking a durable camper's objectives — the anti-camper play that wave-81 contest/deny lacked because the model only DENIED the camper's primary, never scored the taker. Even-handed.

simulator.secondary_area_denial.quoted_text: Area Denial: 2VP if one or more units from your army are within 3" of the centre of the battlefield and there are no enemy units within 3" of the centre; or 5VP if one or more of your units are within 3" of the centre and there are no enemy units within 6" of the centre.
simulator.secondary_area_denial.trigger: end of each battle round, evaluating the scoring army's and the opponent's unit positions relative to the battlefield centre (width/2, height/2)
simulator.secondary_area_denial.effect: Requires one of your units within 3" of centre; then 5 VP if no enemy unit within 6" of centre, else 2 VP if no enemy unit within 3" of centre, else 0. Implemented in Battle._score_area_denial (env-gated SWEG_TIER_A). Even-handed centre-control reward.

simulator.secondary_assassination_tactic.source: https://wahapedia.ru/wh40k10ed/the-rules/chapter-approved-2025-26/ (Chapter Approved 2025-26 Tactical Mission card — verbatim text captured from a prior Wahapedia read; DNS may be unreachable from agent worktrees)
simulator.secondary_assassination_tactic.rule_name: Assassination (Chapter Approved 2025-26 Secondary Mission, Tactical version)
simulator.secondary_assassination_tactic.quoted_text: One or more enemy CHARACTER models were destroyed this turn. TACTICAL 5VP
simulator.secondary_assassination_tactic.trigger: end of each battle round, when a TACTICAL-track army's held Assassination card is scored: one or more enemy CHARACTER units were destroyed this round
simulator.secondary_assassination_tactic.effect: Flat 5 VP if one or more enemy CHARACTER models were destroyed this turn (regardless of wound tier or count). Distinct from the Fixed version (4 VP per 4+-wound CHARACTER, 3 VP per under-4-wound CHARACTER, per unit). Implemented in score_round_delta when tactical=True, routed from Battle._score_one_card when scoring_army.secondary_track == 'TACTICAL'. Env-gated SWEG_TAC_DECK; OFF leaves the Fixed per-unit path byte-identical.

simulator.secondary_bring_it_down_tactic.rule_name: Bring It Down (Chapter Approved 2025-26 Secondary Mission, Tactical version)
simulator.secondary_bring_it_down_tactic.quoted_text: One or more enemy MONSTER or VEHICLE units were destroyed this turn. TACTICAL 4VP
simulator.secondary_bring_it_down_tactic.trigger: end of each battle round, when a TACTICAL-track army's held Bring It Down card is scored: one or more enemy MONSTER or VEHICLE units were destroyed this round
simulator.secondary_bring_it_down_tactic.effect: Flat 4 VP if one or more enemy MONSTER or VEHICLE units were destroyed this turn (regardless of wounds total or count). Distinct from the Fixed version (2 VP base +2 at 15+ wounds +2 at 20+, per unit, no round cap). Implemented in score_round_delta when tactical=True, routed from Battle._score_one_card when scoring_army.secondary_track == 'TACTICAL'. Env-gated SWEG_TAC_DECK; OFF leaves the Fixed per-unit path byte-identical.

simulator.secondary_cull_the_horde_tacti.rule_name: Cull the Horde (Chapter Approved 2025-26 Secondary Mission, Tactical version)
simulator.secondary_cull_the_horde_tacti.quoted_text: One or more enemy INFANTRY units with a Starting Strength of 13+ were destroyed this turn. TACTICAL 5VP
simulator.secondary_cull_the_horde_tacti.trigger: end of each battle round, when a TACTICAL-track army's held Cull the Horde card is scored: one or more enemy INFANTRY units with Starting Strength 13+ were destroyed this round
simulator.secondary_cull_the_horde_tacti.effect: Flat 5 VP if one or more enemy INFANTRY units with Starting Strength 13+ were destroyed this turn (regardless of count). Distinct from the Fixed version (5 VP per qualifying unit destroyed, no per-round cap). Implemented in score_round_delta when tactical=True, routed from Battle._score_one_card when scoring_army.secondary_track == 'TACTICAL'. Env-gated SWEG_TAC_DECK; OFF leaves the Fixed per-unit path byte-identical.

simulator.tactical_deck_big_game.source: https://wahapedia.ru/wh40k10ed/the-rules/chapter-approved-2025-26/ and https://wahapedia.ru/wh40k10ed/the-rules/pariah-nexus-battles/ (durability fidelity wave, audit C divergence 2, verified 2026-07-03 against the printed Chapter Approved 2025-26 / Pariah Nexus Secondary Mission deck; corroborates the wave-181 verbatim capture already cited at simulator.secondary_bring_it_down_tactical / simulator.secondary_assassination_tactical)
simulator.tactical_deck_big_game.rule_name: Bring It Down and Assassination as Tactical-deck cards (Chapter Approved 2025-26 Secondary Mission deck)
simulator.tactical_deck_big_game.quoted_text: Bring It Down -- TACTICAL: One or more enemy MONSTER or VEHICLE units were destroyed this turn. 4VP. When Drawn: If there are no enemy MONSTER or VEHICLE units on the battlefield, you can discard this card and draw a new Secondary Mission card. / Assassination -- TACTICAL: One or more enemy CHARACTER models were destroyed this turn. 5VP.
simulator.tactical_deck_big_game.trigger: battle start, when a TACTICAL-track army's Secondary Mission deck is built (Battle._init_tactical_deck / secondaries.TACTICAL_DECK_POOL)
simulator.tactical_deck_big_game.effect: Every card in the printed CA-2025-26 Secondary Mission deck carries both a Fixed scoring box and a Tactical scoring box; Bring It Down and Assassination are NOT Fixed-exclusive. The wave-119 TACTICAL_DECK_POOL comment asserting the opposite was a divergence from the printed deck (durability fidelity wave, audit C, docs/_DURA_AUDIT_C_POINTS_OUT.md divergence 2): the Tactical scoring for both cards was fully implemented and cited since wave 181 (Battle._score_one_card's is_tactical branch, code/simulator.py:3616-3633) but unreachable, because no TACTICAL-track army could ever draw either card. This gate (SWEG_TACDECK_BIG_GAME, default ON) adds secondaries._BIG_GAME_DECK_CARDS (bring_it_down, assassination) to TACTICAL_DECK_POOL so the existing, already-cited scoring path actually runs; `=0` restores the pre-fix pool byte-identically (no perturbed shuffle order, no extra random consumption). APPROXIMATION: the printed per-card 'When Drawn' redraw-if-no-valid-target clause (quoted above for Bring It Down; Assassination has no such clause) is not separately modelled for the initial draw -- matching the sim's existing treatment of the other kill cards already in the deck (no_prisoners has no When Drawn text) -- because in practice every catalogued army fields at least one CHARACTER and the vast majority field a MONSTER or VEHICLE, so the redraw fires rarely enough not to bias the measured deltas. Cull the Horde is explicitly OUT of scope for this gate: its Tactical text is already cited at simulator.secondary_cull_the_horde_tactical but is likewise unreachable via the same TACTICAL_DECK_POOL exclusion -- left for a separate, self-contained follow-up per CLAUDE.md rule fourteen (keep pull requests small) rather than folded in here.

simulator.secondary_establish_locus.rule_name: Establish Locus (Chapter Approved 2025-26 Secondary Mission, Tactical — action-based)
simulator.secondary_establish_locus.quoted_text: ESTABLISH LOCUS (ACTION) STARTS: Your Shooting phase. UNITS: One unit from your army. COMPLETES: End of your turn, if that unit is within your opponent's deployment zone or within 6" of the centre of the battlefield. IF COMPLETED: Your unit establishes a locus. VICTORY POINTS WHEN: End of your turn. Your unit established a locus this turn and is within 6" of the centre of the battlefield. 2VP OR Your unit established a locus this turn and is within your opponent's deployment zone. 4VP
simulator.secondary_establish_locus.trigger: After the Movement phase, a surplus unit (chaff per strategy._is_chaff_unit) starts the Establish Locus action in the Shooting phase. The action completes at end of turn if the unit is alive AND is within the opponent's deployment zone (4 VP) or within 6" of the battlefield centre (2 VP). While performing the action the unit cannot shoot or declare a charge (core Actions rule); the action fails if the unit moves.
simulator.secondary_establish_locus.effect: 2 VP at end of turn if the performing unit is within 6" of the battlefield centre when the action completes; 4 VP instead if the unit is within the opponent's deployment zone. Rewards pushing expendable bodies into the midboard or beyond — an action-economy tax a low-model durable army (Imperial Knights) cannot pay but a horde or multiple small unit army can, because the performing unit is locked out of shooting and charging for the turn. Even-handed: the same card is offered to both players; the asymmetry falls out of unit count and surplus chaff, not faction. Subject to the 40 VP secondary total cap. SWEG_SECONDARY_PURSUIT positional filter (Battle._assign_establish_locus_actions): without it, the action-assignment step flagged ANY spare unit passing the _unit_can_perform_action contract, including one nowhere near either scoring position — a measured diagnostic put the resulting real achieve rate at 6.1%, the worst in the deck. With the package gate on, assignment re-uses this same scorer's positional test (enemy deployment zone or within 6" of the battlefield centre) at assignment time, immediately after the Movement phase, so only a spare unit that is ALREADY standing where the card pays is ever committed to the action.

simulator.secondary_recover_assets.rule_name: Recover Assets (Chapter Approved 2025-26 Secondary Mission, Tactical — action-based)
simulator.secondary_recover_assets.quoted_text: RECOVER ASSETS (ACTION) STARTS: Your Shooting phase. UNITS: Two or more units from your army, if each of those units is wholly within a different one of the following areas: your deployment zone; No Man's Land; your opponent's deployment zone. COMPLETES: End of your turn, if either two or three of those units are on the battlefield. IF COMPLETED: Those units recover assets. VICTORY POINTS WHEN: End of your turn or the end of the battle (whichever comes first). Two of your units recovered assets this turn — 3VP. Three or more of your units recovered assets this turn — 5VP. When Drawn: If you are playing an Incursion mission, or if there are fewer than three units from your army on the battlefield, you can discard this card and draw a new Secondary Mission card.
simulator.secondary_recover_assets.trigger: At the start of the Shooting phase, two or more surplus units each commit to the Recover Assets action, each unit being wholly within a different one of: own deployment zone, No Man's Land, opponent's deployment zone. The acting units cannot shoot or declare a charge that turn (standard 10th-edition action restriction). At the end of the turn, surviving units that are still on the battlefield and still within their designated area have recovered assets.
simulator.secondary_recover_assets.effect: 3 VP if exactly two units recovered assets this turn; 5 VP if three or more units recovered assets this turn. Scored at end of turn (or end of battle, whichever is first). The Tactical discard condition (Incursion mission or fewer than three army units on the battlefield) means this card is only ever held by armies with broad rosters — an emergent action-economy tax that falls out of unit count, not faction. A low-model durable army (e.g. Imperial Knights) with fewer than three units available cannot satisfy the two-unit minimum across three distinct zones without committing units it cannot spare from the firefight; a horde or multiple small units army routinely has surplus bodies already forward, so it completes this naturally.

secondaries.a_tempting_target.quoted_text: Secondary Mission A TEMPTING TARGET An opportunity to seize a valuable asset has been identified, but the enemy are likely to use it as bait in a trap. Move to secure the site, but be wary of enemy ambushes. When Drawn: Your opponent must select one objective in No Man's Land to be your Tempting Target objective marker. ANY BATTLE ROUND VICTORY POINTS WHEN: End of either player's turn. You control your Tempting Target objective marker. 5VP
secondaries.a_tempting_target.trigger: End of either player's turn; card must be active (drawn and held); the scoring player must control the designated Tempting Target objective marker (a No Man's Land objective selected by the opponent at draw time)
secondaries.a_tempting_target.effect: Score 5 victory points. No Action performed — pure objective-control check at end of turn.

simulator.secondary_card_pursuit_ai.source: https://wahapedia.ru/wh40k10ed/the-rules/chapter-approved-2025-26/ (Chapter Approved 2025-26 Tactical Missions Secondary Mission deck, the same source already cited for simulator.tactical_secondary_deck)
simulator.secondary_card_pursuit_ai.rule_name: Tactical Missions Secondary Mission cards (Chapter Approved 2025-26) — card-pursuit piloting heuristic
simulator.secondary_card_pursuit_ai.quoted_text: When you muster your army, you must decide whether you will be using Fixed Missions or Tactical Missions for the battle. ... Those two Secondary Missions are active for you until you achieve them.
simulator.secondary_card_pursuit_ai.trigger: SWEG_SECONDARY_PURSUIT default-off (implies SWEG_TAC_PURSUE; see Battle._tac_pursue_enabled); a TACTICAL-track army's Movement phase, before the move loop, for each held card with a movement-pursuable geographic condition (behind_enemy_lines, engage_on_all_fronts, cleanse, and the five board take-and-hold cards routed through Battle._board_pursuit_goals) that a SPARE chaff unit (strategy._is_chaff_unit; not already acting, not already assigned) can be routed toward.
simulator.secondary_card_pursuit_ai.effect: ARTIFICIAL-INTELLIGENCE PILOTING HEURISTIC — not a 10e rules claim in itself; grounds in the quoted fact that a Tactical Missions army holds active Secondary Mission cards it is actively trying to achieve every turn, exactly as a real player manoeuvres spare bodies to satisfy the card in hand rather than leaving their positioning to chance. WHICH spare unit is sent and WHERE is not specified by any rule and is decided entirely by this heuristic (Battle._assign_card_pursuit, wave 121, extended here with an Engage on All Fronts branch): it sets Unit.pursue_target, which code/strategy.py pick_move_intent reads as a high-priority override ahead of every other move-intent branch (CAPTURE, STEAL, Fall Back, kiting) so the unit heads straight for the card's geographic goal that activation. Even-handed: no faction branch, no model-count branch — a low-model army with no spare chaff routes nothing and stays faithfully unhelped, exactly as SWEG_TAC_PURSUE's own wave-121/122 build. Deterministic and free of any global `random` draw (pure geometry against already-known board state), so the paired common-random-number evaluation's downstream stream is unaffected relative to itself. Implemented in Battle._assign_card_pursuit / _board_pursuit_goals, read by strategy.pick_move_intent's pursue_target override.

simulator.am_secondary_pursuit.rule_name: Tactical Missions card pursuit — Astra Militarum army-scoped entry point (artificial-intelligence piloting heuristic)
simulator.am_secondary_pursuit.quoted_text: Grounded in the Tactical Missions mechanic itself (players draw Secondary Mission cards and play toward them): a real player routes spare units to score their active cards. Not a new rules claim — the cards and their scoring conditions are separately cited in this file.
simulator.am_secondary_pursuit.trigger: SWEG_AM_SECONDARY_PURSUIT=1 (default-off while screening); the SWEG_SECONDARY_PURSUIT package's gate reads accept the acting army and also enable when that army's faction is Astra Militarum
simulator.am_secondary_pursuit.effect: ARTIFICIAL-INTELLIGENCE PILOTING, army-scoped per the Principle-2 recipe proven by simulator.am_advance_discipline: the universal package (establish-locus positional filter + card-pursuit movement + your-turn-only voluntary discard) screened Astra Militarum +5.17 toward its real 45.3 but fed the over-credited factions (Necrons +4.89, Chaos Daemons +5.80; headline +0.46), so the universal gate is HELD and the built-for faction's lift banks army-scoped. Off path (both gates unset) byte-identical.

simulator.tactical_when_drawn_redraw.source: https://wahapedia.ru/wh40k10ed/the-rules/chapter-approved-2025-26/ (Chapter Approved 2025-26 Secondary Mission deck; per-card When Drawn clauses re-verified verbatim against Wahapedia this session, 2026-07-03)
simulator.tactical_when_drawn_redraw.rule_name: Secondary Mission cards — the printed 'When Drawn' redraw clauses (Chapter Approved 2025-26)
simulator.tactical_when_drawn_redraw.quoted_text: Cull the Horde -- When Drawn: If there are no enemy units on the battlefield that satisfy the condition below, you can discard this card and draw a new Secondary Mission card. / Bring It Down -- When Drawn: If there are no enemy MONSTER or VEHICLE units on the battlefield, you can discard this card and draw a new Secondary Mission card. / Behind Enemy Lines, Defend Stronghold, Storm Hostile Objective, Display of Might -- When Drawn: If it is the first battle round, draw a new Secondary Mission card and shuffle this card back into your Secondary Mission deck. / Marked for Death -- When Drawn: ... If there are no units from their army on the battlefield, discard this card and draw a new Secondary Mission card. / Recover Assets -- When Drawn: If you are playing an Incursion mission, or if there are fewer than three units from your army on the battlefield, you can discard this card and draw a new Secondary Mission card. / Assassination -- (no When Drawn clause; the audit's aside that Assassination carries one was checked and is incorrect per the printed card, which has no When Drawn box.)
simulator.tactical_when_drawn_redraw.trigger: battle start (opening 2-card deal, Battle._init_tactical_deck) and each round's redraw refill (Battle._score_tactical_hand) and the New Orders / voluntary-discard refill, when a TACTICAL-track army draws a Secondary Mission card whose printed When Drawn condition is met. Env-gated SWEG_TAC_SHEDDING (default ON); D1a of docs/_SEC_ECONOMY_AUDIT.md.
simulator.tactical_when_drawn_redraw.effect: The simulator dealt the Tactical hand blind and only ever discarded a card it ACHIEVED, so a card drawn against a board that cannot satisfy it (Bring It Down with no MONSTER/VEHICLE, Cull the Horde with no 13+ INFANTRY, a first-battle-round positional camp card) clogged the 2-card hand for the game (docs/_SEC_ECONOMY_AUDIT.md §2, §5). Battle._when_drawn_clause / _draw_tactical_card now fire each printed When Drawn clause at draw time: a 'discard'-clause card whose target does not exist is dropped and the next drawn; a first-battle-round 'shuffle_back' positional card is returned to the deck and the next drawn. `=0` restores the blind deal byte-identically (the helper reduces to deck.pop(0), so the opening hand is deck[:2] and the remainder deck[2:] exactly as before). DETERMINISM: no global RNG is consumed — the draws come off _init_tactical_deck's private zlib.crc32-seeded shuffle, and 'shuffle back into your deck' is modelled as a deterministic bottom-insert (a documented approximation that avoids a fresh reshuffle) with a per-draw guard so the loop always terminates. Marked for Death's no-enemy-units clause and Recover Assets' fewer-than-three-units clause are implemented but practically never fire in a 2000-point game.

simulator.new_orders_stratagem.source: https://wahapedia.ru/wh40k10ed/the-rules/chapter-approved-2025-26/ (Chapter Approved 2025-26 core Secondary Mission stratagem; text re-verified verbatim against Wahapedia this session, 2026-07-03)
simulator.new_orders_stratagem.rule_name: New Orders (Chapter Approved 2025-26 core Secondary Mission stratagem)
simulator.new_orders_stratagem.quoted_text: NEW ORDERS -- 1CP -- Core Stratagem -- Strategic Ploy Stratagem. WHEN: End of your Command phase. TARGET: One of your active Secondary Mission cards. EFFECT: Discard it and draw one new Secondary Mission card.
simulator.new_orders_stratagem.trigger: End of each of a TACTICAL-track army's Command phases (Battle._apply_new_orders, called from Battle._run_round immediately after the command-phase command-point award). Env-gated SWEG_TAC_SHEDDING (default ON); D1c of docs/_SEC_ECONOMY_AUDIT.md.
simulator.new_orders_stratagem.effect: The army spends 1 command point to discard one active Secondary Mission card and draw a replacement (through _draw_tactical_card, so the fresh card's own When Drawn clause fires). The stratagem is the canonical command-point tool a real Tactical player pays for to cycle a dead card, which the simulator spent nothing on (docs/_SEC_ECONOMY_AUDIT.md §4). WHICH card to swap and WHETHER to spend the point is an artificial-intelligence piloting decision the stratagem does not specify: the heuristic fires at most ONCE per Command phase, and only on a STRUCTURALLY DEAD held card (_tac_card_structurally_dead: the card's qualifying kill target / objective marker / Objective-Control-capable actor no longer exists, so it can never score again this battle) when the army has a command point to spare — swapping a provably-dead card is correct play even under the tight, deliberately un-doubled command-point budget (D4 command-point-generation doubling is out of scope for this fix wave), so it never starves a defensive stratagem of a point it would otherwise have used. Deterministic and free of the global RNG. `SWEG_TAC_SHEDDING=0` disables it byte-identically (the method early-returns before touching any state).

simulator.actions_hand_gated.source: https://wahapedia.ru/wh40k10ed/the-rules/chapter-approved-2025-26/ and https://wahapedia.ru/wh40k10ed/the-rules/core-rules/#Actions (Actions core rule; Tactical Missions hold at most two active cards at a time)
simulator.actions_hand_gated.rule_name: Actions performed only for a held Secondary Mission (Chapter Approved 2025-26 Tactical Missions + core Actions rule)
simulator.actions_hand_gated.quoted_text: If you are using Tactical Missions ... you have at most two active Secondary Mission cards at any time. ... While a unit is performing an Action, that unit is not eligible to shoot or declare a charge. [Cleanse and Sabotage each 'START: Your Shooting phase', so the performing unit is spent for the turn.]
simulator.actions_hand_gated.trigger: After the Movement phase, when a Tactical-track army decides whether to commit a unit to the Cleanse or Sabotage action (Battle._assign_cleanse_actions / _assign_sabotage_actions). Env-gated SWEG_ACTIONS_HAND_GATED (default ON); D2 of docs/_SEC_ECONOMY_AUDIT.md.
simulator.actions_hand_gated.effect: A unit is only pulled out of shooting and charging to perform an action for a Secondary Mission the army can actually score, i.e. one it HOLDS. The assignment step previously gated on `chosen_secondaries`, which for a TACTICAL army is the whole drawable pool (secondaries.pick_secondaries returns tuple(TACTICAL_DECK_POOL) for a Tactical army), not the two-card held hand the scorer credits — so the simulator assigned Cleanse and Sabotage every round regardless of whether the card was in hand, forgoing shooting for cards that could never score (docs/_SEC_ECONOMY_AUDIT.md D2: 958 Cleanse and 2260 Sabotage assignments realised only 172 and 300 victory points, ~0.18 and ~0.13 per action). Battle._action_card_available now gates a Tactical army on `tactical_hand`; a FIXED army's `chosen_secondaries` already IS its two-card hand, so its behaviour is unchanged. `SWEG_ACTIONS_HAND_GATED=0` restores the legacy `card in chosen_secondaries` membership byte-for-byte. Recovers the wasted actions and the kills the forgone shooting cost, which also lifts every other secondary that depends on those kills.
